messages:
maria: Quick question — for service->service auth in multi-tenant flows, are we leaning to 'credential attachment' (API keys carrying project metadata) or 'claim-based' ephemeral tokens (short-lived JWTs with project claim)? need to decide for next sprint.

sam: Claims. better for cross-project and revocation. downside: signing/introspection infra.

jen: Attachment is simplest for internal-only calls. But if a key leaks it's tied to project forever unless we rotate.

li: FYI the current proxy adds ~2ms for an authz hop if we do remote introspection. Perf matters for short LLM inference calls.

maria: Right. thinking hybrid: long-lived API keys for intra-project/local-only ops, and short-lived JWTs for cross-project or external integrations. keep verification local where possible.

neil: +1 hybrid. Suggest token `aud` pattern to avoid wildcard acceptance: `redwood:svc:{svc-id}:proj:{proj-id}`. also include `exp` and `kid`.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary: jwt-validation-hook v0.3 deployed to staging :white_check_mark:

sam: For RBAC mapping, prefer model: claims -> principal -> roles. that decouples tokens from policy lifecycle. API keys can map to service-actor aliases for legacy.

jen: Agree. But add aliasing layer so infra teams can bind many keys to a single role set without editing policies constantly.

li: Perf mitigation: cache JWKS and token->principal resolution in proxy with short TTL (30-60s). avoid blocking calls on every request. Also expose metrics for cache hit rate.

maria: Good. Concrete next steps: write an RFC that covers: token JSON format, header conventions (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer`, `X-Project` fallback), verification path (local verify -> cache -> introspect fallback), cache TTLs, RBAC mapping semantics, migration strategy for existing API keys. volunteers?

sam: I'll draft token format + signing key rotation plan.

jen: I'll own RBAC mapping, alias semantics and policy examples.

li: I'll run a proxy perf baseline and propose cache defaults.

neil: I'll draft migration strategy and rollout flags (feature gate per-service).

maria: Thanks — let's aim to have a draft by Thu EOD, sync Fri 10am to review. :calendar: 

maria: One more quick note — avoid adding a ton of new runtime introspection RPCs; prefer push of signing keys to edge where safe.

sam: ack. we'll document trust boundary clearly.

jen: And include skip-list for internal-only paths to keep latency tight.

li: will add perf numbers to the RFC.

neil: I'll add migration checklists for infra teams and a rollback plan.

maria: Great, closing loop here. If anyone has short UX questions for service owners, ping me. :thumbsup:
